info.desc: Discovery is the second studio album by the French house duo Daft Punk, released in March 2001. It marks a shift in the sound from Chicago house, which they were previously known for, to disco, post-disco and synthpop-inspired house. The album provided itself as a soundtrack to the anime film Interstella 5555: The 5tory of the 5ecret 5tar 5ystem, which was a collaboration between the creators of the album, Leiji Matsumoto, and Toei Animation. All of the music videos for the tracks on the album are segments of the film. Interstella 5555 follows a story of a kidnapped extraterrestrial band. .

podcast.body: Beyond its visual counterpart, "Discovery" exerted significant influence on the future of pure musical trends. "El Discovery marcaba muchísimas influencias en el futuro de la música, al mejor no está parte del visual, pero si la parte musical más pura."

Daft Punk's "Discovery" was a very solid album, characterized by a well-defined and coherent concept. The accompanying film, "Interstella 5555," served as a crucial narrative thread that greatly enhanced the understanding of this ambitious musical project. "Era un disco muy sólido, con una idea muy cerrada y muy coherente y que tener toda esta película le daba un hilo conductor a todo que nos ayudaba mucho más a entender el proyecto del discobre, que era realmente ambicioso."

Daft Punk's album *Discovery*, released in 2001, is highlighted as one of the most important albums of the last 25 years. It was recorded with absolute saturation of Auto-Tune and played a significant role in popularizing the use of Auto-Tune as a stylistic element in music. "en el 2001 uno de los discos más importantes de los últimos 25 años que es el discobre y de dad punk que está grabado en absoluta saturación de auto-tium y que además por ni a demodar el auto-tium no solo él."

podcast.body: For their second album, recorded at Daft House (a studio built in Thomas's bedroom in Paris — the gear took up so much space he had to move the bed), Guy-Manuel and Thomas shifted toward a slicker sound incorporating post-disco and R&B, samples from the late 1970s and early 1980s techno-pop era (Depeche Mode, OMD, Thomas Dolby, Erasure), vintage synthesizers, and Auto-Tune. The album had more song structure than Homework. The lead single "One More Time" had been sitting around since 1998 before being resurrected. "Digital Love" sampled "I Love You More" by American songwriter and producer George Duke. The fiction of the robot transformation — the sampler explosion at 9:09am on September 9, 1999 — emerged around this time, tied to the debut of the helmets. "Their gear took up so much space that he had to move the bed somewhere else."

podcast.body: Released a few years after "homburmo," this album achieved unprecedented mass success worldwide. It attracted a very commercial audience, described as "unfaithful," and was stylistically quite distinct from their previous work. The commercial success of "bril" contrasted with the critical acclaim of "homburmo," placing the band in a "no man's land" between commercial and critical appeal. "un éxito de masas impresedentes."

podcast.body: This album was presented not in a conventional manner, but as a comprehensive audiovisual project, "Interstella 5555", following their previous work, "Homeward". "Daphpank presentaban nuevo trabajo que era el Discovery y no lo presentaban al uso, sino que lo presentaban con todo un proyecto audiovisual que era todo este proyecto de interés de la 5555."

Upon its release, "Discovery" left many critics horrified due to its powerful disco passages, prominent vocoders, and particularly its heavily saturated autotune. Despite this initial negative reception, these very elements became foundational in contemporary music, influencing artists such as The Weeknd and Drake, demonstrating how the album set a direction not clearly perceived at the time. "Mucha de la crítica se quedaba verdaderamente horrorizada. Teníamos esas pasas tan potentes en la música disco, tenemos esos vocoders y tenemos, sobre todo, ese auto tiene un tan saturado que aparte de la crítica había dejado horrorizado y que hoy es una de las bases de música."
